previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma was admitted for her 21st cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She reported feeling well with no neurological or systemic symptoms. The chemotherapy was administered safely with urine alkalinization maintained throughout. She received fosaprepitant for nausea prophylaxis due to prior headaches with Zofran, and experienced mild nausea on day two, which resolved with ativan and compazine. Her methotrexate level at 36 hours was 0.13 micromolar, indicating safe clearance. A brain MRI showed no evidence of lymphoma recurrence, with only stable chronic changes. She remained neurologically and hematologically stable. Aspirin was held during admission and restarted at discharge, with heparin bridging for DVT prophylaxis. She was discharged home in stable condition with a short course of oral leucovorin and instructions to continue her regular medications for chronic pain, asthma, and depression.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Patient with lymphoma for further evaluation and followup.  

TECHNIQUE:  T1 sagittal and axial, and FLAIR, T2, susceptibility and diffusion
axial images of the brain were acquired before gadolinium.  T1 axial and i
MPRAGE sagittal images obtained following gadolinium with axial and coronal
reformats.  

COMPARISON:  Comparison was made with the previous MRI examinations of ___ and 9 and a 1,013.  

FINDINGS:

There has been no significant interval change since the previous studies. 
Encephalomalacia in the right frontal lobe region seen with ex vacuo
dilatation of the anterior horn of the right lateral ventricle.  There is no
abnormal enhancement seen in this region.  

There is no mass effect, midline shift or hydrocephalus.  There are no acute
infarcts seen.  There are no chronic micro hemorrhages. 

Following gadolinium administration there is no evidence of abnormal
parenchymal, ossicular or meningeal enhancement seen.

The vascular flow voids are maintained.  Mucosal thickening is seen in the
visualized paranasal sinuses as noted previously.  

IMPRESSION:

No significant interval change since the previous MRI examinations.  No
enhancing brain lesions are seen.  No new abnormalities are noted.
